details:
When an avatar contact doesn’t react, there’s currently no easy way to find out why. The output log doesn’t record who touched a contact, or whether that person was allowed to, so creators and users are left guessing whether the cause is the avatar setup, a safety setting, or a permission.

Request: when a contact on the local player’s avatar is touched, write a log line that includes:

- The name and user ID of the player who touched it

- The contact receiver’s name

- Whether that player had permission to trigger it, and if not, which setting blocked it

Why this helps:

- Troubleshooting: users can see straight away whether a contact was blocked or never touched at all.

- Creators: it’s much easier to support people using their avatars when “it doesn’t work” can be checked in a log.

- OSC and companion apps: tools that read the log could tell who an interaction was with. Today they can only guess from who’s in the instance.

Keeping it manageable: contacts can fire many times a second, so one line when a touch starts would be enough. This could sit behind a debug logging option, or only cover the local player’s own avatar, to keep logs small and limit what’s recorded about other players.

Example (the format is only a suggestion, styled after VRChat’s existing log lines, not something VRChat logs today):

```

2026.11.03 21:14:02 Debug      -  [AvatarDynamics] Contact touched: Head_Pat by Ember Fox (usr_bbbbbbbb-1111-2222-3333-444444444444) | Allowed: true

2026.11.03 21:14:37 Debug      -  [AvatarDynamics] Contact touched: Head_Pat by Grey (usr_cccccccc-1111-2222-3333-444444444444) | Allowed: false (blocked by: contact permissions)

```
title: Logs should report more Contact Info
